messages:
From: Elliot Barnes <elliot@orchid.io>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 3 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: EIN tokenization question for vendor onboarding

Hi Ben + Monica,

Thanks for the portal invite — we walked Orchid through the vendor profile but ran into a validation block when submitting our W-9: the portal rejected the full TIN storage option. Your guide mentioned Redwood supports an EIN tokenization option to avoid storing raw TINs. Can you confirm what evidence you need so we can complete onboarding without exposing the full EIN in your system?

What we can provide right away:
- Signed W-9 (I attached a PDF with the EIN redacted and a copy with full at our side)
- A redacted bank letter showing the entity name and last four of the EIN (attached)
- Ability to sign a DocuSign envelope that includes an electronic notarization step

Is DocuSign KBA + redacted bank letter acceptable for a tokenization flow, or do you require a notarized physical letter? Also let us know whether the tokenization API will require additional identity verification from the signatory (driver's license scan, KBA, etc.).

We want to keep the PO timeline moving — if we can finish this this week we can accept the draft PO terms.

Cheers,
Elliot Barnes
Head of Finance, Orchid Analytics
Orchid Analytics | elliot@orchid.io

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 3 Apr 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: EIN tokenization question for vendor onboarding

Hi Elliot — thanks for the quick note and for attaching the docs.

Short answers up front:
- We can accept a tokenization workflow so Redwood does not retain the raw EIN.
- DocuSign with KBA is our preferred path for US entities; it provides an auditable signature chain.
- We typically require either (a) a bank letter with the entity name and partial EIN (last 4) or (b) a notarized W-9. The redacted bank letter usually suffices when paired with DocuSign KBA.

Two small asks before we start tokenization:
1) Please confirm the signatory on the W-9 (name and title) and that they match the DocuSign signer.
2) Provide the bank letter as a PDF with letterhead (you did this — thanks) and, if possible, include the contact name/phone for the bank rep for us to validate if we need to.

If you confirm, I will loop in Procurement (Karthik) to kick off the tokenization envelope and Docusign KBA flow. Once tokenized we will mark the vendor as tax-verified and proceed to create the PO (we can attach a draft PO to the DocuSign packet so paperwork aligns).

Tentative ETA: tokenization + validation in 24–48 business hours after we get confirmation and the DocuSign completes.

Ben Carter
Senior Procurement Specialist | Redwood Inference
